conversation.content:
Good morning! I’m so glad you’re here. I’m Sarah, a perinatal mental-health clinician, and my job is to listen—really listen—to how you’re doing since your baby arrived. Today we’ll use a short, well-studied questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply ten questions about your mood, thoughts, and energy over the past week; it helps us spot anything that might benefit from extra support. Everything you share stays between us unless you or your baby’s safety is at immediate risk, and you can pause or skip anything you need. When you’re ready, we’ll move through the questions together at your pace.

To begin: in the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

I’ve actually found it pretty hard to laugh lately. Most of the time when my partner or the sitcom we usually watch tries to be funny, I just don’t feel it. I’d say only occasionally—maybe once or twice in the past week—have I managed a real laugh, and even that felt kind of forced.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not very often… I’d say only once or twice this whole week, and even then the laugh didn’t last long. Mostly I feel like I’m just going through the motions.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park—but now it’s like, why bother? I can still feel a flicker of “that might be nice,” but it fades fast. Honestly, I’d say only a couple of times this week have I actually looked forward to anything, and even those moments felt pretty dim.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” It’s happened maybe three or four nights this week—I catch myself thinking I’m a lousy mom even when everyone says it’s normal newborn stuff.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. My mind keeps spinning through “what-ifs” about the baby—like, is he breathing when he’s napping, or am I burping him right? I’ll be folding laundry and suddenly feel my heart racing for no real reason. It’s not constant, but it hits several times a day and is hard to shut off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

It’s happened a few times—maybe three nights this week. I’ll just be rocking the baby, everything quiet, and suddenly my chest feels tight, like I can’t get a full breath. There’s no real danger, but for a minute I’m convinced something awful is about to happen. It passes after a bit, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days it feels like I’m drowning in small stuff. The dishes pile up, the baby needs feeding, and I just freeze, thinking, “I can’t handle one more thing.” I still push through, but it’s like walking in wet cement—everything’s heavier and slower.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I’ve definitely had trouble sleeping. It takes me forever to drift off because my head keeps circling through everything I might’ve messed up that day, and once I’m out I still wake up once or twice with those anxious thoughts buzzing. So I’d say most nights this week I’ve lost at least a couple hours of real sleep because I just feel so low and worried.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the week, yeah. I wake up feeling heavy, like there’s a weight on my chest, and it sticks around even when nothing bad is happening. I wouldn’t say it’s every single minute, but more days than not I just feel sad or empty.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

It’s happened twice this week—once in the middle of the night when the baby wouldn’t latch, and again yesterday evening when my mom pointed out I hadn’t eaten all day. Both times the tears just came, and once I started I couldn’t stop for a little while.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

A couple of fleeting thoughts have popped up—like when I’m really overwhelmed at 3 a.m. and the baby won’t settle, I’ll think, “What if I just weren’t here?” But there’s no plan, no urge to act on it; it’s more a scared, exhausted wish to escape for a second. It’s happened maybe once or twice in the past week, and I push it away fast because it frightens me.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 22: Screening Note – Postpartum Mood (non-diagnostic)

Patient-reported symptoms (past 7 days):
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, frequent tearfulness  
- Daily anxiety (racing heart, “what-ifs”), 3 panic-like episodes (chest tightness, breathlessness)  
- Self-blame/guilt re: parenting competence; feels “drowning” in routine tasks  
- Initial- and middle-insomnia linked to ruminative worry  
- Fleeting passive suicidal ideation (no plan/intent)

Pattern: Symptoms present most days, causing subjective impairment in coping and sleep.

Screening significance: High endorsement of depressive and anxiety items; passive SI noted → safety concern. Recommend prompt formal assessment (PHQ-9/EPDS, clinical interview) and safety planning.
